title: Identity and access with IAM
summary: IAM controls who can do what in AWS. A policy grants actions on resources. Least privilege means granting only needed actions.
introduction: IAM controls who can do what in AWS. A policy grants actions on resources. Least privilege means granting only needed actions. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain identity and access with iam
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: IAM controls who can do what in AWS. A policy grants actions on resources. Least privilege means granting only needed actions.

blocks.code:
Reader needs: read one approved object
Reader does not need: change account settings or delete a bucket
blocks.title: Identity and access with IAM

blocks.text: A small permission scope limits mistakes. A real policy must name the intended actions and resources.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Describe the minimum job of a read-only reviewer.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not practise with root-account access or put credentials in source files.
For more detail later, use this [AWS further reading](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/aws-overview/introduction.html).
